note: Sentence Studio data. Colloquial spoken forms only (Bangalore Kannada, Delhi Hindi, Chennai Tamil), romanized Latin, never native script, no plural suffixes for beginners. Verb forms are built as stem plus ending in lib/grammar.ts and agent/teacher.py from the tables below. Music verbs and vocabulary come first on purpose. No em dashes anywhere.

verbs.note: an instrument. In Bangalore people also say piano play maadtini; in Chennai piano play pannuren.
In Kannada and Hindi the word for song and the verb sing are the same word.
English word plus the do-verb. This pattern works for hundreds of actions.
kelu is the same word in Kannada and Tamil.
The master verb. English word plus this verb makes almost any action.
The formal words are pravaasa (kn), safar (hi), payanam (ta); on the street everyone says travel.
a game or sport, not an instrument
togo (take) also means buy in Bangalore speech.
wait maadu, wait karna, wait pannu are just as common.

music.trick: haadu sounds like had to: a song you HAD to sing. paattu: PUT two hands together and sing.
Kannada and Hindi use the same word for song and sing. Tamil flips one letter: paattu (song), paadu (sing).
bajaana sounds like bhajan: you play for a bhajan. vaasi: VAAsi sounds like vibe-see.
Everyone says music. Sangeeta and sangeet are the formal words; isai is the Tamil one you see on posters.
Sa Re Ga Ma is the same in every Indian language. Sur is the short Hindi form: sur mein means in tune.
Taala means clap. Keep the taala means keep the beat.
Same root everywhere. Kannada and Tamil add a vowel or an m at the end, Hindi drops it.
dhun sounds like done: once the dhun is stuck in your head, you are done.
awaaz: a-VOICE with the v softened. kural: the voice that CURLs out of your throat.
bega and vegama share a root: be quick. tez means sharp and fast, like a knife.
dheere dheere is the famous Bollywood slowly slowly. medhuva sounds like mellow.
jor and zor both mean force. saththama: with SOUND.
mellage: MELLOW-ge. Hindi and Tamil reuse their slow word for soft.
innomme is innu plus omme: one more. thirumba means turn back.
modalu and modhal both mean first. shuru is start, like shuru karo, let us start.
Everyone says practice. Riyaaz is the classical musician's word in Hindi and you will hear it in music circles.
kelu is identical in Kannada and Tamil. sunna: sounds like soon-ah, listen soon.
dhyaan is attention, the same word as meditation.
mele and mela both mean up or above. Music teachers in India mostly say high in English.
neeche means below. kelage and keezha mean down.
Students say sir or miss in all three languages. Guru ji is warm and respectful in Hindi.
Everyone says student. Shishya is the classical guru-shishya word.
Same word. To class: class-ge (kn), class (hi), class-ku (ta).
Kacheri is the Carnatic word for a concert in both Kannada and Tamil.
baansuri comes from baans, bamboo. Kannada and Tamil speakers mostly say flute.
Instrument names are the same everywhere. Only the verb changes: nudisu, bajaana, vaasi.
chennaagi and nalla both mean well. Say it after a good take.
chennaagide is the all-purpose Kannada word for it is good. nalla irukku is the Tamil twin.
swalpa, thoda, konjam all mean a little. The teacher's most useful word.
nillisi and niruthunga share the nil root, to stand still.
iri and irunga both come from iru, to be or stay.
gino sounds like gin-oh: count the gin bottles.
Count in before every take. ek do teen chaar is the count-in every Bollywood drummer knows.

numbers.trick: ondu and onnu both start like ONE.
Hindi do: two things to DO. eradu and rendu rhyme.
teen as in thirTEEN. mooru and moonu are twins.
naal in Kannada and Tamil. chaar sounds like char: four charred toast slices.
paanch: a PUNCH with five fingers.
aaru is identical in Kannada and Tamil. chhe: six is what you say when you sneeze, chhe.
aath and eight sound almost the same. entu and ettu too.
nau is nine with the vowel bent. ombattu and onbadhu are twins.
das like decimal. hattu and patthu differ by one letter.
bees: twenty bees. ippattu is two tens squeezed together.
mu (three) plus the tens ending in both Kannada and Tamil.
pachaas: pach (five) plus aas. A fifty rupee note is pachaas ka note.
nooru is identical in Kannada and Tamil. sau sounds like so: so many, a hundred.
eshtu is also how much. kitne: kit-nay, how many kits?

fruits.trick: hannu and pazham end many fruit names: maavina hannu, maampazham.
kela sounds like kayla with a banana. baale and vaazhai are the same word said in two accents.
aam: I AM the king of fruits. maa is the root in Kannada and Tamil.
seb and sebu are cousins. Tamils just say apple.
santra: SANTa brought oranges. Most people say orange.
draakshi and dhraatchai share one root. angoor: on-GOOR, hang on the vine.
papeeta and pappaali both keep the pap sound.
tarbooz and tharboosani are twins. kallangadi is the odd one out.
thenga is coconut in the south; kaayi means the raw fruit.
nimbe and nimbu are cousins. elumichai is the Tamil one you hear at every juice stall.
anaar: an ARR of ruby seeds.
amrood: am-ROOD, a rude green fruit.
halasu and palaa share the la sound; the jackfruit is huge, so the word is short.

vegetables.trick: kaayi at the end of a Kannada or Tamil word usually means a raw vegetable.
pyaaz: PIE-aaz. eerulli: EAR-ulli, an onion in your ear.
tamaatar is tomato with an Indian accent. thakkaali sounds like tackle-y.
aaloo: everyone knows aaloo paratha. Kannada aalu plus gadde, a root.
gaajar ka halwa is the dessert. Kannada and Tamil just say carrot.
baingan bharta is the dish. kathirikkaai: cat-tree-kaai.
mirch is hot, like mirchi. milagu is pepper, milagaai is chilli.
adrak chai is ginger tea. inji sounds like ginger with the g dropped.
ulli means onion family: eerulli onion, bellulli garlic (white onion).
saag paneer is the dish. soppu and keerai are the leafy bundles at the market.
kottambari and kothamalli are twins. dhaniya: DUN-ya, sprinkle on everything.
patta means leaf, gobhi means the cauliflower family.
gobhi manchurian is the street snack.
matar paneer. batani and pattaani are cousins.
bende and venda are the same word in two accents. bhindi masala.
murungakkaai sambar: the long green stick in your sambar.

countries.trick: desha and desh are the same word. naadu is in Tamil Nadu itself: the Tamil country.
yaava, kaun sa, endha all mean which. The first question any stranger asks.
Everyone says India. Bhaarat is the formal name you hear in the news.
dinda, se, la irundhu all mean from. Swap the country and the line works for anywhere.

countries.en: America, England, Australia, Germany, Japan, China, Dubai, Singapore
countries.trick: Country names stay English in daily speech. Only the word for country and from changes.
vi plus desh: another country. veli means outside in Tamil.
videshi is what the auto driver calls a tourist.
shehar: shah-hair, the city of the shah. nagara is in Bengaluru's Jayanagar.
halli ends many Kannada place names: Marathahalli, Nagarbhavi halli.
bhaashe and bhaasha are twins. mozhi is the Tamil word, as in Tamil mozhi.

questions.trick: idu enu, yeh kya hai, idhu enna: point at anything and ask.
elli and enga end in the same open sound. kahaan: ka-HAAN, where oh where.
kab: as in cab, when is the cab coming. eppo: e-PO, when do we go.
yaaru is the same in Kannada and Tamil.
yaake: ya-KAY, why. kyun rhymes with soon.
hege: heh-GAY. eppadi: e-PADI, how did you paddle here.
eshtu and evlo are your market words.
Kannada reuses eshtu; Hindi bends kitna to kitne; Tamil has ethana.
yaavudu: which one of these. kaun sa: who-ish one.
gante, baje, mani all mean the bell, o clock.
aaytu and aachu both mean it became.
Your rescue line in every class. andre = if you say.
Literally what do they say for ___.
howdu (yes) plus aa becomes really? Say it with raised eyebrows.

little.trick: nanna piano, mera piano, en piano. Hindi picks mera or meri by the thing.
nimma hesaru enu, aapka naam kya hai, unga peru enna.
One letter shorter than the polite form in Kannada and Tamil.
avan (he) plus a or oda.
Hindi uska covers both his and her.
namma Bengaluru, namma metro: you already know this one.
avru (they) plus a.
manege, ghar ko, veetukku: to home.
Bangalore-alli, Delhi mein, Chennai-la.
India-inda, India se, India-la irundhu.
nanna jote, mere saath, en kooda: with me.
nanagaagi, mere liye, enakkaaga: for me.
tea mattu coffee, chai aur coffee, tea-um coffee-um.
aadre: AH-dray. aana: but also means elephant, say it fast.
why plus if-you-say: yaake plus andre.
naanu koodaa, main bhi, naan-um: me too.
maatra and mattum are cousins.
tumba chennaagide, bahut achha, romba nalla.
The politeness word. Put it in front of any request.
eega: EE-ga, now. ippo: ip-PO, now.
aamele: after that.
when plus also: yaavaga plus lu, eppo plus um.
always plus not.

describe.trick: dodda mane, bada ghar, periya veedu: before the noun.
olle kelsa, achha kaam, nalla velai: good work.
Say it is not good rather than bad; it is what natives do.
bisi bele bath is hot lentil rice. garam masala.
hosa varsha, naya saal, pudhu varusham: new year.
hale and pazhaya are the same word said two ways.
Everyone says costly in the south.
kammi means less; kammi maadi = reduce it.
sari also means okay. Sari sari = okay okay.

time.trick: do pahar: two watches of the day.
sanje: SAN-jay. shaam: like the name Sham.
Hindi kal is both yesterday and tomorrow; the verb tense tells you which.
naale and naalaikku share a root.
hafta comes from haft, seven in Persian.
Days in Kannada and Hindi end in vaara. Most people just say Monday.
guru is Jupiter, the teacher planet.
bhaanu and ravi both mean sun.
The same bell word means hour.
kabhi kabhi is a famous film title.
dina dina, roz roz: day after day.

kn.title: The verb goes last
kn.body: Say who, then what, then the action. English word order is I play piano; Kannada is I piano play.

kn.title: One ending per person
kn.body: Learn the ending once and put it on every verb: tini (I), tiya (you), tira (you polite), tane (he), tale (she), tivi (we), tare (they).

kn.title: Future is free
kn.body: Spoken Kannada uses the present form for the future. The time word does the work.
kn.example: naale nudistini = I will play tomorrow

kn.title: Past endings
kn.body: Past stem plus e (I and you), ri (you polite), a (he), lu (she), vi (we), ru (they).

kn.title: Not: alla and lilla
kn.body: Now or future: verb plus alla. Past: verb plus lilla. Same word for every person, no endings to learn.
kn.example: nudisalla (do not play), nudislilla (did not play)

kn.title: Question: stretch the last sound
kn.body: Turn the last vowel into aa and it becomes a question. No extra word needed.

kn.title: The Bangalore shortcut
kn.body: English word plus maadu works for almost any action. Locals do it all day.

kn.title: To and in
kn.body: ge means to, alli means in or at. No gender on I, you, or we. Keep nouns singular; beginners do not need plural endings.

hi.title: The verb goes last
hi.body: Who, then what, then the action, then the little helper word.

hi.title: Gender is yours
hi.body: A man says bajaata, karta, jaata. A woman says bajaati, karti, jaati. This is the ending people notice first.
hi.example: main gaati hoon (woman), main gaata hoon (man)

hi.title: The helper word closes it
hi.body: hoon with main, ho with tum, hain with aap, hum, ve, hai with he or she.
hi.example: tum bajaate ho, voh bajaata hai

hi.title: Past with ne
hi.body: Doing-verbs take ne in the past and the verb matches the thing: maine piano bajaaya, maine chai pi. Go and come skip ne: main gaya, main gayi.

hi.title: Future endings
hi.body: unga or ungi (I), oge (tum), enge (aap, hum, ve), ega or egi (he, she).

hi.title: Not and question
hi.body: Put nahin before the verb for not. Put kya at the start for a yes or no question.

hi.title: Right now
hi.body: raha or rahi plus the helper word means doing it at this moment.

hi.title: Want and can
hi.body: mujhe X chaahiye for a thing, main X karna chaahta hoon for an action, mujhe X aata hai for I know how.

ta.title: The verb goes last
ta.body: Who, then what, then the action.

ta.title: One ending per person
ta.body: ren (I), re (nee), reenga (neenga), raan (he), raa (she), rom (we), raanga (they). Put it on every verb.

ta.title: Past endings
ta.body: Past stem plus en, e, eenga, aan, aa, om, aanga.

ta.title: Future endings
ta.body: A v or pp sound, then the same endings as the past.

ta.title: Not: maatten and la
ta.body: Will not or do not: the to-form plus maatten. Did not: the to-form plus la. Same for every person.

ta.title: Question: add aa
ta.body: Add aa to the end of the verb. Politeness lives in nga: use neenga and the eenga ending with anyone older or unknown.

ta.title: The Chennai shortcut
ta.body: English word plus pannu works for almost any action.

ta.title: To and in
ta.body: ku means to, la means in or at. No gender on I, you, or we. Keep nouns singular.

frames.why: Liking sits with the person: to-me ___ is liked. No verb ending to learn.
Same frame, flipped with illa, nahin, or aadhu.
Want and need share one word in Kannada and Tamil.
beda and vendaam are the polite everyday no thanks.
Having is near-me ___ exists. hatra, paas, kitta all mean near.
illa and nahin hai turn any is into is not.
Kannada and Tamil ask by stretching the last sound to aa; Hindi puts kya in front.
The most useful word in the market.
Thing first, then where, then is.
Point and ask. eshtu and evlo also mean how many.
swalpa, thoda, konjam soften any request into a please.
Kannada and Tamil need no word for is; this plus the thing is a full sentence.
Add the aa sound to the noun to ask.
tumba, bahut, romba mean very. Say it after a good take.
Your bargaining line. jaasti is shared by Kannada and Tamil.
Places carry their own to: manege, class-ge, veetukku, class-ku.
Knowing sits with the person, like liking and wanting.
gottilla and theriyaadhu are the honest beginner lines.
Polite you: nimage, aapko, ungalukku.
ona, karte hain, laam turn any action into a let us. practice maadona, chalo practice karte hain, practice pannalaam.

commandNote.kn: Polite ends in i (nudisi, banni, kodi); a friend or a child gets the bare verb (nudisu, baa, kodu). Do not: verb plus beda (nudisbeda).
commandNote.hi: Polite ends in iye (bajaiye, aaiye, dijiye); friends get o (bajaao, aao, do). Do not: mat before the verb (mat bajaao).
commandNote.ta: Polite ends in nga (vaasinga, vaanga, kudunga); friends get the bare verb (vaasi, vaa, kudu). Do not: verb plus aadheenga (vaasikkaadheenga).
